calls.beyond: Ottawa is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 171 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 114 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Cousins scores with a little over two minutes left to lift the Senators
paras: Fabian Zetterlund struck first for the Senators on the power play early in the first, but Clayton Keller made it 1-1 for Utah four and a half minutes later. It was a busy third period. Michael Amadio put the Senators back ahead 2-1 early in the period. Barrett Hayton tied it up for Utah less than four minutes later, but the Mammoth didn’t score again. Nick Cousins put the Sens ahead for good with a little over two minutes left, and Shane Pinto added the empty-netter with 16 seconds left to make it 4-2.

The Senators were outshot 32-21, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. Samuel Ersson made 30 saves for the Senators, and Karel Vejmelka stopped 17 of 20 at the other end. The Senators moved to 11-6-1, fourth in the Atlantic, while the Mammoth fell to 10-7-1, slipping to fifth in the Central.

items.text: Tim Stützle passed Alexei Yashin for fifth on the Senators’ all-time assists list, with 274.
Clayton Keller has a point in five straight games.
Mikhail Sergachev’s nine-game point streak ended.
The Mammoth were without Kailer Yamamoto, Nate Schmidt and John Marino. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team was missing more at the time.
